text:
maya: Heads up — saw a ~3x 99p latency spike on prod-rt yesterday (~03:20 UTC). Timeline and SLO graphs point to eviction stalls; sampler enters a slowpath and stays there for ~30s. Logs attached to the incident but copying key traces here. Anyone else see this?

ian: saw it in canary too (~03:15). FIFO policy seemed to recover faster than LRU for the same load, FWIW. Reinsert churn + repeated victim selection.

raj: minimal repro I used locally: `./tools/kv_pressure.py --policy lru --burst 1000 --ctx_len 512 --duration 300` — reliably hits a 99p jump from ~150ms -> ~450ms.

devon: quick profiling snapshot from a repro run:
```\n└─evicter::sample_slowpath 48%\n  ├─evicter::choose_victim 30%\n  ├─kv::reinsert 22%\n  └─pager::writeback 12%\n```
Also observed heavy contention on `evicter::handshake_mutex`.

elaine: reminder — we merged `adaptive_sampling` in last month. It flips into sampling when hotset_ratio > 80%. Could be too eager under sustained bursts :thinking: 

maya: @devon can you paste the flamegraph snippet you saw in prod?

devon: pasted above. additionally, stack traces from prod show repeated `choose_victim` calls with almost identical keys — points to fragmentation + reinserts causing hot entries to be churned.

ian: metrics: `metrics.kv.fragmentation` spiked ~2.4x before the latency jump, then gradually declined. Also `evicter.sampling_count` spiked.

raj: ran FIFO under same synthetic workload: 99p ~180ms, LRU ~450ms. Tradeoff: FIFO increased total bytes paged out by ~30% and long-run memory churn is higher.

elaine: options on the table:
- raise sampling trigger threshold (80% -> 90%)
- add a cooldown so we don't re-enter sampling repeatedly (e.g., 60s)
- move victim selection to an async path (do heavy work off the request path)
Which should we try first?

maya: propose a 3-way bisect in canary: (A) threshold -> 90%, (B) cooldown 60s, (C) async victim selection. Schedule perf jobs and compare 99/99.9p + page-out bytes + CPU.

perf-bot: Scheduled perf job #4567: `kv-evict-threshold-90` on canary
perf-bot: Scheduled perf job #4568: `kv-evict-cooldown-60` on canary
perf-bot: Scheduled perf job #4569: `kv-evict-async-select` on canary

devon: I can prototype the cooldown quickly. Tiny diff:
```
// pseudocode
if (now < last_sampling_time + cooldown_secs) return; // skip heavy sampling
last_sampling_time = now;
perform_sampling();
```
should avoid repeated slowpath re-entries. I'll add metrics for `sampling_cooldown_hits`.

ops-bot: Rolled canary with cooldown patch to cluster-rt-canary-3 at 05:10 UTC.

ian: early canary numbers: cooldown patch reduced 99p by ~2.2x and flattened spikes. Throughput drop ~4% under microbench. Flamegraph still shows `sample_slowpath` but much less frequent.

maya: good. Action items: @devon open PR with tests and metrics, @raj run a 6hr soak and capture paging/fragmentation metrics, @elaine add dashboard+alert for sampling events, I'll draft a short postmortem if soak is clean.

raj: 6hr soak started 05:30 UTC, pushing logs to the incident folder. Will ping if it reappears :eyes:.

devon: PR opened — #7890 — adds cooldown, emits `sampling_count` and `sampling_cooldown_hits`, and includes a unit test that simulates repeated bursts.

elaine: I'll add alert: `evicter.sampling_rate > 0.5/s` sustained over 5m -> P1. Also add a panel for `sampling_cooldown_hits` so we can see how often cooldown prevents resampling.

maya: :thumbsup: If soak stays green we'll merge cooldown to prod-rt next deploy. If not, we'll test async victim selection from perf job #4569. Thanks all. (reaction: :rocket:)
